newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp - financial policy hindering growth.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp - financial policy hindering growth.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday German financial policy was slowing economic growth and that the country should use the flexibility already contained in the Maastricht Treaty to spur growth.
"Financial policy is hindering still continuing economic recovery," he said.
"There can be no doubt that a consolidation of the budget is needed. But commitment to consolidation should also keep the economic situation in consideration," Krupp said.
A copy of his speech was distributed to the media in advance.
In order to qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), the German government is introducing extra taxes this year and ponderng ways to restrain government spending.
Both policies threaten to remove money from the economy that would otherwise be used to fan economic growth.
But Krupp, who is also president of the state central bank in Hamburg, Schleswig Holstein and Mecklenburg Vorpommern, said the Maastricht Treaty leaves room for interpreting deficit targets flexibly.
According to the Treaty, countries wishing to join EMU must slash their deficit to gross domestic product ratios to three percent. In 1996, Germany's ratio was 3.9 percent.
But the Treaty leaves soom room for countries to qualify for EMU even if they do not exactly meet that target as long as they are making progress towards that goal.

"It is therefore regrettable that German financial policy does not make use of flexibility in the Maastricht Treaty," he said. "For good reason, the Treaty does not require an exact landing on the fiscal criteria."
